title: Smart warehousing
introen: Rack systems, automated high-bay storage and mezzanine columns across the warehouse.

scenes.title: Warehouse racking
scenes.en: Keep an inclination history for selected pallet-rack uprights across the warehouse. Link each reading to the rack row and bay, then compare it with the installation reference, documented load states and handling reports. The record gives the warehouse team a consistent way to review orientation after layout changes, reported forklift contact or rack maintenance alongside its normal inspection process.
scenes.pointen: A rigid upright position protected from pallet loads and forklift contact.
scenes.briefen: Rack layout, upright section, typical load states, required angle sensitivity and inspection workflow.
scenes.alten: A wide warehouse aisle with orange pallet-rack beams, blue uprights and stored goods.
scenes.source: V3 medium-precision application copy; broad first-version industry imagery retained.
scenes.objectiveen: Keep an inclination history for selected pallet-rack uprights across the warehouse.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of a selected rack upright relative to its documented installation reference.

scenes.en: Connect local upright-orientation readings to the rack rows and service locations of an automated high-bay warehouse. Maintenance teams can compare the angle history before and after stacker-crane servicing, rack adjustments or reported contact, using consistent loading conditions. The named monitoring points keep the information useful across a large storage installation while leaving crane, shuttle and load clearances available.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid upright position outside stacker-crane, shuttle and load clearances.
scenes.briefen: Rack height, row identifiers, service access, load states, smallest useful angle change and fixing position.

scenes.source: V3 medium-precision application copy; broad first-version industry imagery retained.
scenes.objectiveen: Connect local upright-orientation readings to the rack rows and service locations of an automated high-bay warehouse.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of a selected high-bay upright under comparable loading conditions.

scenes.title: Cantilever racking
scenes.en: Follow the orientation of selected cantilever-rack columns carrying tubes, timber or other long goods. Associate each point with its bay, arm arrangement and normal load distribution so later readings can be compared meaningfully. The resulting angle record supports review after handling impacts, rack adjustments or changes in stored lengths and weights, with the required sensitivity defined for the installation.
scenes.pointen: A rigid column section clear of cantilever arms, long goods and loading contact.
scenes.briefen: Column and base details, arm layout, representative loads, access and required angle sensitivity.
scenes.alten: Cantilever storage racks with long goods, upright columns, projecting arms and floor-mounted bases.
scenes.imagebrief: Fixed cantilever racks storing long steel tubes or timber; visible uprights, arms and anchored bases.
scenes.source: V3 medium-precision application copy; broad first-version industry imagery retained.
scenes.objectiveen: Follow the orientation of selected cantilever-rack columns carrying tubes, timber or other long goods.
scenes.measureen: Inclination of the selected cantilever-rack column under comparable loading.

scenes.title: Drive-in pallet racking
scenes.en: Organize upright-inclination records by storage lane in drive-in or drive-through pallet racks. Compare readings with the installation reference and documented loading sequences to review changes after reported forklift contact, support-rail adjustment or maintenance. Recording the same structural member under comparable loads helps the inspection team relate an angle change to a specific lane rather than an unidentified part of the warehouse.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid upright position outside vehicle travel and pallet-support clearances.
scenes.briefen: Lane layout, loading sequence, upright identity, review sensitivity and inspection access.
scenes.alten: Drive-in pallet racking with deep storage lanes, upright frames and horizontal pallet-support rails.
scenes.imagebrief: Complete drive-in pallet lanes with supporting rails and intact loaded pallets; show entry lane and anchored steel upright frames.
scenes.source: V3 medium-precision application copy; broad first-version industry imagery retained.
scenes.objectiveen: Organize upright-inclination records by storage lane in drive-in or drive-through pallet racks.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of a selected drive-in rack upright at documented load conditions.

scenes.en: Associate inclination readings with the columns supporting a warehouse mezzanine or storage platform. Establish the reference after installation and record representative loads on the level above. Later comparisons provide an orientation history for review after storage-layout changes, equipment relocation or support maintenance, keeping each reading linked to the column grid and the owner’s inspection records.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid column position protected from handling contact and clear of removable finishes.
scenes.briefen: Column grid, mezzanine use, representative loads, fixing permission and required angle sensitivity.

title: Poles & towers
introen: Street lighting, power lines, telecom sites and roadside sign supports.

scenes.title: Street-light poles
scenes.en: Keep a named inclination reference for street-light poles across roads and public spaces. Maintenance teams can compare later readings after reported vehicle contact, foundation works or pole servicing, with each record tied to the same fixing direction and asset identifier. The approach also applies to selected roadside equipment poles where a local orientation history is useful for planned inspection and maintenance.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid pole section above the base and protected from vehicle contact.
scenes.briefen: Pole material and diameter, base arrangement, measurement direction, access and required review sensitivity.

scenes.objectiveen: Keep a named inclination reference for street-light poles across roads and public spaces.

scenes.title: Transmission towers

A documented reference supports comparisons after foundation works, member replacement or scheduled inspections. Keeping the angle history with maintenance and site-condition records helps the utility review a persistent local change at the intended member, using the angular sensitivity specified in its asset monitoring plan.

scenes.briefen: Tower drawings, member and elevation, electrical clearances, required angle sensitivity and inspection workflow.

scenes.objectiveen: Relate orientation readings from selected transmission-tower members to the tower identifier, mounting level and measurement direction.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of an approved tower member along defined measurement axes.

scenes.title: Telecom towers
scenes.en: Maintain a local orientation history for selected telecom-tower members as equipment and site arrangements change. Link every point to its mounting height, measurement direction and tower reference, then compare readings with antenna additions, maintenance visits and foundation inspections. The record helps the site team distinguish a persistent change at a named structural member from an undocumented change in the measurement setup.
scenes.pointen: A rigid structural member clear of antenna adjustments, equipment access and service routes.
scenes.briefen: Tower type, member geometry, mounting height, work history, required angular change and access.
scenes.alten: A telecommunications lattice tower with cellular antenna panels against the sky.

scenes.objectiveen: Maintain a local orientation history for selected telecom-tower members as equipment and site arrangements change.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of an approved telecom-tower member at a defined height.

scenes.title: Billboard support poles
scenes.en: Connect the inclination history of a billboard support pole to the sign location and its maintenance record. Compare the same member and measurement direction after panel replacement, support work or foundation servicing, noting the relevant wind and loading conditions. This gives the sign owner a repeatable local angle reference for inspection review without confusing changes in the billboard panel with changes in its support.

scenes.briefen: Support geometry, panel dimensions, base details, environmental context and required angle sensitivity.

scenes.measureen: Inclination of the selected billboard-support pole at the approved mounting position.

scenes.en: Organize inclination records for selected distribution poles by asset number and line section. Compare the local pole angle with its installation reference after nearby ground works, pole maintenance or reported contact, using the same measurement direction. A consistent point record gives the utility team useful context for field inspections across dispersed routes and helps connect an observed change to the correct pole.

scenes.briefen: Pole material, line section, fixing approval, relevant angle change, service access and inspection schedule.

title: Bridges, roads & ports

scenes.title: Bridge piers & structural members
scenes.en: Keep an angle record for a named bridge pier or other selected rigid member during agreed installation, maintenance or inspection stages. Connect each reading to its fixing direction, reference condition and relevant work records. H310-TS150M is an option where the engineering team’s local rotation objective is compatible with ±0.1° accuracy; the record complements the bridge’s established survey and inspection measurements.

scenes.briefen: Member drawings, measurement direction, reference stages, required rotation sensitivity and engineering review procedure.
